title: Two Americans Win the Nobel Prize in Economics
summary:
Two economists born in the United States, Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, have won this year's Nobel memorial prize in economics. The winners were announced Monday in Stockholm, Sweden.

Economics is the study of how people, businesses and governments make choices about money, jobs and goods. Hall and Woodford built models that help governments and central banks deal with sudden changes in the economy, such as an energy crisis.

The prize group said the winners helped "smooth out the economy's peaks and troughs." That means their work helps keep the economy from swinging too far up or down.

In the 1970s, many countries had high prices and high unemployment at the same time. That showed older ideas were too simple. Working separately, Hall and Woodford made better models based on how people and businesses really decide to spend.

Woodford said winning was "a tremendous honour" and "a surprise." The prize is presented on Dec. 10.
why_it_matters: When the economy stays steadier, families have an easier time keeping jobs and paying for things they need.
